companyDescription: Commercial + defense launch + lunar services · NASA $13M SkyFall Mars aeroshell subcontract Jul 7 · Alpha Block 2 / VICTUS HAZE Sep 30 · SciTec Golden Dome SHIELD IDIQ
priceNote: Fell 8.3% Jul 7 despite the positive SkyFall news — broad risk-off in speculative space names + profit-taking after the recent NASA CLPS run. Now ~14x FY26E revenue vs RKLB ~65-70x, a wider value gap than a week ago.
summary: Firefly won a $13M NASA JPL subcontract (Jul 7, 2026) to build the aeroshell for the SkyFall Mars mission (three heritage Mars helicopters, targeted late-2028 launch) — another proof point for its multi-mission platform after the $144M Blue Ghost CLPS win on Jul 2. The stock still fell 8.3% on the day, part of a broader speculative/space-name pullback rather than a company-specific issue. 11 analysts hold a Moderate Buy with an average PT of $42.20 (+64% from here); Needham's Space & Industrial Summit (Jul 9) and Q2 earnings (est. mid-Aug, unconfirmed) are the next catalysts, with the VICTUS HAZE Block 2 launch (Sep 30) remaining the binary event.

catalysts.name: NASA JPL $13M SkyFall Mars Aeroshell Subcontract
catalysts.description: Jul 7, 2026: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory awarded Firefly a $13M subcontract to manufacture, test and deliver the aeroshell for the SkyFall mission — three heritage Mars helicopters performing science and subsurface mapping, targeted for launch in late 2028. Adds to the Jul 2 $144M Blue Ghost CLPS lunar win, extending Firefly's platform to Mars.

catalysts.name: Alpha Block 2 — VICTUS HAZE Launch
catalysts.description: Sep 30, 2026 — US Space Force + DARPA responsive-space mission. First flight of the Block 2 vehicle iteration; the binary event for the DoD-trust thesis.

risks: Stock fell 8.3% Jul 7 despite good news — signals fragile sentiment/positioning in speculative space names right now, not just company execution
Alpha Block 2 first-flight binary — VICTUS HAZE Sep 30 is a new rocket iteration; failure = ~1-year setback + program reset
Q2 earnings date is still unconfirmed/calendar-estimated — a short public reporting history means real surprise risk either way
SpaceX IPO contagion — if SpaceX goes public, institutional capital could rotate out of RKLB/FLY and into SpaceX directly
Cash burn pre-FCF positive — the $420-450M FY guide requires on-schedule execution across NASA, DoD and commercial contracts simultaneously
RKLB competitive overlap on responsive launch + defense contracts

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75%; next FOMC Jul 28-29. FLY's revenue base is NASA/DoD contracts, largely decoupled from consumer/corporate rate sensitivity — but as a pre-FCF small-cap, its cost of any future capital raise is rate-exposed.
macroRisk.inflationNote: June CPI lands Jul 14, six days out — a hot print would reinforce the Fed's hawkish June dot plot and pressure high-beta speculative names like FLY more than it affects the underlying government contract base.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Golden Dome, NATO, and DARPA responsive-launch spending are secular tailwinds largely insulated from the rate cycle. Needham conf (Jul 9) and Q2 earnings are the near-term company-specific triggers.
macroRisk.summary: LOW — the government/defense contract base insulates the underlying business from rates/inflation. The primary near-term risk is launch execution (Block 2) and broad speculative-sector sentiment, not macro.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Commercial/defense launch names typically rally 10-20% in the 2-3 weeks before a mission milestone or major contract award. Firefly has strung together two NASA wins in a week (Blue Ghost Jul 2, SkyFall Jul 7) — normally a pre-run setup, though this time the market sold the news instead.

postWin.note: Blue Ghost Mission 1's successful lunar landing (Mar 22, 2026) — first commercial lunar landing ever — drove Firefly +24% in 3 days. The SkyFall/Blue Ghost 2028 contract wins are smaller-dollar but reinforce the same platform-validation thesis.

postLose.note: Firefly's Alpha Vehicle 2 partial failure (Oct 2022) sent the stock down roughly 25% and delayed the program about 18 months. A VICTUS HAZE Block 2 failure in Sep 2026 would likely be of similar magnitude.

spotSizing.reason: Two NASA contract wins in a week (Blue Ghost + SkyFall) reinforce the multi-mission platform thesis even though the stock sold off — moderate speculative sizing 4-6%, add after Needham conf/Q2 confirmation.

comparableCases.event: Blue Ghost Mission 1 — First Commercial Lunar Landing
comparableCases.note: Blue Ghost Mission 1 successfully landed on the Moon on March 22, 2026 — first-ever commercial lunar landing. Stock +24% in 3 days, the template for how the market rewards a proven mission milestone.

Two positive NASA contract announcements in a week (Jul 2 Blue Ghost CLPS, Jul 7 SkyFall aeroshell) were both sold into — a reminder that in a risk-off tape, even genuine fundamental wins can be overwhelmed by sector-wide profit-taking.
